messages:
alex: Heads up — seeing a cluster-wide spike in local SSD write latency on gpu-pool-* after the nightly large-batch inference rollouts. IOPS near queue depth and nodes are entering degraded state.
jen: :eyes: which metric? io.wait or device io? can you paste the panel?
alex: Device write latency and nvme write queue depth. Grafana: gpu-pool-2 avg write_iops went from 20k to 140k around 03:12 UTC, sustained for ~6m.
raf: That matches reports from the provisioning jobs — they push big microbatched KV cache checkpoints every ~5m. Might be write-amplification + GC on drives. We saw similar pattern but not this magnitude.
alex: Posting short logs from one node:
```
[2026-03-18T03:12:14Z] nvme0n1: write latency 95ms qdepth 256
[2026-03-18T03:12:20Z] firmware: async GC triggered, lane busy
[2026-03-18T03:12:40Z] kernel: writeback: force page cache flush
```
sylvia: SMART shows rising media_error_count on a few hosts (nvme SMART log 1/3). Not full failure yet but trending.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3381 - nvme write surge in gpu-pool (link: https://incident.internal/INC-2026-3381)
jen: Ok. Quick mitigations we can do now: 1) throttle batching on rollout jobs 2) reduce concurrent ephemeral-cleaner workers 3) temporarily divert new workloads to other regions.
raf: I can patch the rollout config to reduce --batch-size and add a jitter. Example patch:
```
kubectl -n infra patch cm rollout-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"inference_batch_size":"64","max_concurrent_batches":"4"}}'
```
alex: Also lowering ephemeral-cleaner concurrency helped in the past. Current job is set to 50 workers; suggest 8.
sylvia: I'll run an agent to lower concurrency on the cleaner k8s CronJob.
ops-runbooks: Runbook: storage/gc-thrashing suggests: 1) reduce producer burst 2) apply controller-level slow_down via /etc/insights/drive-throttle.conf 3) schedule targeted node eviction 4) enable fallback caching. Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/storage/gc-thrashing
jen: For immediate node protection we should cordon the worst hosts, drain, then rotate them out of the pool until SMART stabilizes. Use `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` on drain because these are ephemeral nodes.
raf: I'll start evict on the top 6 effected nodes. Command:
```
kubectl drain ip-10-0-23-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```
alex: Rolling evicts will create load elsewhere; we should temporarily increase capacity in dedicated pool or enable spillover to another region (ops approved for 2h).
jen: I'll open a quick request to autoscaler to allow +6 nodes in ephemerals for 2h.
infra-bot: Autoscaler request submitted: ASR-2026-771 - allow +6 ephemeral gpu nodes for 2h
sylvia: After drains started, write_iops dropped ~60% on affected hosts. SMART counters still incrementing but rate slowed.
raf: Long-term: need to change checkpoint strategy — incremental checkpoints and staggered flush windows. I'll file a proposal and link it here.
raf: Proposal draft: use async KV shard flush with per-shard backpressure, add randomized flush windows across hosts, add an emergency controller that postpones flush when nvme queue > 200.
alex: Good. Also evaluate cheaper NVME profiles with better sustained write endurance for ephemeral tier.
jen: Can someone run a quick SMART export for the rotated nodes and attach? we should track which drives to RMA.
sylvia: Attached SMART dump to the incident and flagged 4 drives for replacement.
alex: Thanks all. Short checklist saved to incident: 1) throttled rollouts 2) lowered cleaner concurrency 3) drained top hosts 4) temporary capacity increase 5) file long-term KV flush proposal. Will monitor for next 3 hours and update.
jen: :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-3381 updated: remediation actions in progress.
raf: Leaving a note — avoid changing fstrim cadence during high-burst windows; it can spike I/O by forcing block reclaim.
alex: Agree. We'll add that to runbook amendments.
jen: If metrics look stable in 30m we can gradually re-enable previous concurrency.
sylvia: Metrics trending down. Closing loop in 2hrs unless new alerts.
ops-runbooks: Reminder: postmortem template link: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/template-storage
alex: Thanks team, will ping again if anything flares up.
